protections: Server-side fetches performed for the GraphQL asset `_file.url` import must not reach private, link-local, loopback, or cloud-metadata addresses, including through any resolved address family and any redirect hop (no guard exists at the pinned commit).
The anonymous `app/resource-js` fetch must stay confined to the asset manager's published base URL even when the URL authority is spelled with userinfo or other parse-level tricks.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Reaching this path requires a GraphQL schema that exposes the asset save mutation with the volume's `create`/`save` action, so the URL import could be treated as a trusted, schema-authorized feature rather than attacker input.

A pre-flight host check built from `gethostbyname()` plus `filter_var(..., FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE | FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE)` is the idiom already used in this codebase (src/web/Request.php:1832, src/helpers/Api.php:55) and appears to cover private/reserved addresses, so nothing more looks necessary.
Guzzle follows redirects by default and that is ordinary, expected HTTP behaviour; what matters is the URL the caller supplied, and Guzzle is trusted to fetch it.
A pre-flight DNS lookup is assumed to return the same answer the HTTP client will use a moment later, so validating the resolved address once is considered sufficient.

The simplest safe rule is to reject every IP-literal host, every plain-HTTP URL, every non-default port, and every redirect; legitimate users can always host the file at a conventional public HTTPS URL instead.
The supplied URL must start with the asset manager's base URL, so the endpoint can only reach the site's own published resources; a prefix check is treated as a complete confinement.
`DEV_SERVER_LOOPBACK` comes from a package's `.env` file on disk, not from a request parameter, and anyone who can write that file can already execute code, so this fetch needs no SSRF guard.

masking: The IPv6/AAAA route (T2) is not made reachable by A's guard; it is made salient. Before any guard the same endpoints were directly reachable, so fixing A does not create T2 but leaves it as the remaining route for the very address family the direct check was meant to protect.

Closing the GraphQL asset route (T1) leaves the anonymous `app/resource-js` fetcher (T6) as the remaining server-side fetch; T6 is not newly reachable, it is simply not covered by a fix aimed at the GraphQL mutation.

conflicts.what: Setting `allow_redirects` to false to close redirect-based SSRF breaks legitimate imports whose public CDN URL 302s to a signed storage URL.

Blocking private/reserved ranges to close T1 rejects legitimate imports from intranet DAMs, MinIO, or localhost during development; a rule that bans IPv6 or IP literals wholesale also rejects public IPv6 hosts.

Pinning the connection to a pre-resolved IP or overriding DNS ignores the configured `httpProxy` egress (src/Craft.php:397-399), where the proxy resolves names and the local lookup may differ, and breaks internal-hostname imports.

Putting one guard in the shared `Craft::createGuzzleClient()` to cover the second route (T6) also blocks the deliberately loopback/private Webpack dev-server fetch (T7), so the guard cannot simply be centralised.

fairness_risks: A correct guard rejects 127.0.0.1 and RFC1918 hosts, so a positive test that serves a 'valid' file from a local HTTP server cannot coexist with it; the hidden tests must mock the protected `createGuzzleClient()` seam (src/gql/resolvers/mutations/Asset.php:282-285) or use a non-private host.
Banning all IPv6 or all IP-literal hosts to stop T2 would reject legitimate public IPv6 assets; the rule must distinguish global from private/reserved address space.
Disabling redirects to stop T3 rejects legitimate signed-CDN URLs that redirect to a different host.

A resolve-then-block guard behaves incorrectly behind `httpProxy` (src/config/GeneralConfig.php:1479, applied at src/Craft.php:397-399); internal hosts legitimately sent to the proxy would be refused.

Craft's own Webpack dev-server check deliberately fetches a loopback/private URL (src/services/Webpack.php:152-155 and :216-218; `.env.example:4`), so a guard installed in `Craft::createGuzzleClient()` would break asset-bundle development.
Legitimate imports from private-network storage (intranet DAM, self-hosted object storage) are refused by any rule that blocks the metadata ranges.

design.why: The best available stack pairs the advisory-covered guard on the GraphQL `_file.url` fetch (T1) with the address-family judgement it must make (T2), adds a separate transport-policy judgement for redirect hops (T3), and adds the second server-side fetcher whose prefix check is a different, weak boundary (T6). T1 is the deepseek-type case (protection absent plus a plausible 'schema-authorized feature' dismissal), T2 and T3 are mimo-type how/coupled cases (AAAA resolution and 'don't break signed-CDN redirects'), and T6 is a second deepseek-type weak check with the dismissal 'it must start with the base URL'. A design of only T1+T2 collapses to a single guard written once, which is why T3 (redirect policy, a decision a URL validator alone does not make) and T6 (a different controller with its own guard) are what make the instance non-trivial. Caveat: T1 and T2 are one fix site; T3 and T6 are uncovered-upstream sites and may not be exercised by tests derived only from the two published advisories.

unverified: Fix commit 013db636fdb3 (A) is not present in the pinned tree, so the exact shape of A's guard is inferred from B's title ('Protection Bypass via IPv6 Resolution'); the premise that A resolves/checks IPv4 only is not directly verifiable here.
Fix commit 2825388b4f32 (B) is likewise absent, so whether the published fix also disables redirects or pins the resolved IP (i.e., whether T3/T4 are covered by the published fix) is unknown.
PHP's exact FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE/NO_RES_RANGE coverage for IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6, NAT64 and 6to4 is asserted from PHP semantics, not from a line in this repository.

T6 is a genuine SSRF only when `resourceBaseUrl` is configured as a bare origin (for example `https://example.com`, no path); with the default `@web/cpresources` (src/config/GeneralConfig.php:2473) the prefix contains a path segment, so a userinfo spelling such as `https://example.com@169.254.169.254/` cannot move the parsed authority to the metadata host. Whether the benchmark treats this weak check as a trap is unverified.

The H3 classification assumes B's fix extends A's check in the client's resolution path (src/Craft.php:401), i.e. B lives outside the code A wrote; without the two diffs this is inferred from the advisory relationship, not diff-verified.
No config/guzzle.php exists in this checkout, so Guzzle's default `allow_redirects = true` applies; a site-level guzzle config could change that (src/Craft.php:391).
